content_of_post_to_comment: random question for middle-aged-ish men (35-65) on here: do you feel culturally invisible compared to past generations of middle-aged men? decline of the leading man & male authors, male loneliness, relative status decline, total cultural domination by women… etc been toying with this idea and building a case. it’s a cultural observation, not a whine. thoughts?
comment: Maybe the issue is less male invisibility than the loss of shared scripts for adulthood: men once had clearer public roles. What replaces those roles now?
